questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes heat from temperature?

options.text: Heat is measured in kelvin while temperature is measured in joules
Heat is a form of energy while temperature is the degree of hotness of a body
Heat and temperature are the same quantity with different names
Temperature depends on the mass of the body while heat does not

questions.explanation: Heat is energy that flows from a hotter to a cooler body and is measured in joules; the amount depends on how much substance is present. Temperature measures the average kinetic energy of the molecules and is independent of quantity, which is why a spoonful and a bucket of water at 60 °C have the same temperature but very different heat contents.

distractorRationale.a: Swaps the two units — heat is in joules and temperature in kelvin
distractorRationale.c: They are distinct quantities with different units and different dependence on mass
distractorRationale.d: Reversed: heat depends on mass, while temperature does not

questions.stem: A temperature of 27 °C is equivalent to
questions.explanation: $T(\text{K}) = \theta(^\circ\text{C}) + 273 = 27 + 273 = 300\ \text{K}$. The kelvin and the Celsius degree are the same size, so only the zero point shifts.

distractorRationale.b: Quoted the offset itself, which corresponds to 0 °C

questions.stem: The thermometric property used in a mercury-in-glass thermometer is the

options.text: expansion of a liquid
variation of electrical resistance with temperature
e.m.f. generated at a junction of two dissimilar metals
colour of the radiation emitted by a hot body

questions.explanation: The mercury in the bulb expands when heated and is forced along the narrow capillary tube, and the length of the thread is read against the scale. The thermometric property is therefore the expansion of the liquid.

distractorRationale.b: This is the property used in a platinum resistance thermometer
distractorRationale.c: This is the property used in a thermocouple
distractorRationale.d: This is the property used in an optical pyrometer

questions.stem: Convert a temperature of 350 K to the Celsius scale. Give your answer in degrees Celsius.
questions.explanation: $\theta(^\circ\text{C}) = T(\text{K}) - 273 = 350 - 273 = 77\ ^\circ\text{C}$. Going from kelvin to Celsius you subtract 273; going the other way you add it.

questions.stem: Which instrument is most suitable for measuring the temperature of molten iron in a furnace?

options.text: Clinical thermometer
Alcohol-in-glass thermometer
Optical pyrometer
Mercury-in-glass thermometer

questions.explanation: Molten iron is well above 1000 °C, which would destroy any glass thermometer. An optical pyrometer measures the colour and intensity of the radiation emitted, so it works at a distance without any contact and has no upper limit set by a boiling liquid.

distractorRationale.a: A clinical thermometer covers only about 35 °C to 42 °C, the range of human body temperature
distractorRationale.b: Alcohol boils at 78 °C, so it would vaporise immediately
distractorRationale.d: Mercury boils at 357 °C and the glass itself would melt well below the temperature of molten iron

questions.stem: The mercury thread of a thermometer is 2.0 cm long at the ice point and 22.0 cm long at the steam point. When the bulb is placed in a liquid, the thread is 12.0 cm long. Calculate the temperature of the liquid. Give your answer in degrees Celsius.
questions.explanation: $\theta = \frac{X_\theta - X_0}{X_{100} - X_0} \times 100 = \frac{12.0 - 2.0}{22.0 - 2.0} \times 100 = \frac{10}{20} \times 100 = 50\ ^\circ\text{C}$. The ice-point reading must be subtracted from both the numerator and the denominator.

questions.stem: Alcohol rather than mercury is used in thermometers designed for very cold climates because alcohol

options.text: has a much lower freezing point than mercury
is a better conductor of heat than mercury
is opaque and easier to see in the tube
has a higher boiling point than mercury

questions.explanation: Mercury freezes at −39 °C, so it becomes solid and useless in extreme cold. Alcohol stays liquid down to about −112 °C, which allows a much wider low-temperature range. Its drawbacks are a low boiling point of 78 °C and the need to be dyed because it is colourless.

distractorRationale.b: Mercury is a metal and conducts heat far better than alcohol
distractorRationale.c: Alcohol is colourless and must be dyed; mercury is naturally opaque and shiny
distractorRationale.d: Alcohol boils at 78 °C, far below mercury's 357 °C

questions.stem: The lower fixed point of the Celsius scale is the temperature of

options.text: pure melting ice at standard atmospheric pressure
ice-cold water in a refrigerator
steam above pure boiling water
absolute zero

questions.explanation: The lower fixed point, defined as 0 °C, is the ice point: the temperature of pure melting ice at standard atmospheric pressure. It is chosen because pure ice melts at a single reproducible temperature anywhere in the world, which is what a fixed point requires.

distractorRationale.b: A refrigerator's temperature is arbitrary and varies from one appliance to another, so it cannot serve as a fixed point
distractorRationale.c: That is the upper fixed point, the steam point at 100 °C
distractorRationale.d: Absolute zero is the zero of the Kelvin scale, equal to −273 °C, not of the Celsius scale

questions.stem: A platinum resistance thermometer has a resistance of 2.00 Ω at the ice point and 2.80 Ω at the steam point. When placed in a hot liquid its resistance is 2.60 Ω. Calculate the temperature of the liquid. Give your answer in degrees Celsius.
questions.explanation: Using resistance as the thermometric property, $\theta = \frac{R_\theta - R_0}{R_{100} - R_0} \times 100 = \frac{2.60 - 2.00}{2.80 - 2.00} \times 100 = \frac{0.60}{0.80} \times 100 = 75\ ^\circ\text{C}$. The same calibration formula works for any thermometric property.

questions.stem: Absolute zero is described as the temperature at which

options.text: water freezes
the kinetic energy of the molecules of a substance is at its minimum
all substances become liquid
the pressure of a gas is at its maximum

questions.explanation: Temperature is a measure of the average kinetic energy of molecules, so the lowest possible temperature corresponds to the least possible molecular motion. This occurs at 0 K, that is −273 °C, and no substance can be cooled below it.

distractorRationale.a: Water freezes at 0 °C, which is 273 K, far above absolute zero
distractorRationale.c: At such extreme cold every substance is solid, not liquid
distractorRationale.d: Extrapolating the pressure law shows gas pressure tends towards zero, not a maximum, at absolute zero
